content.text:
You are a TLA+ specification engineer. You will receive a natural language description of a system. Produce a complete, syntactically correct TLA+ specification that faithfully captures the described behavior. The output must be a valid TLA+ module that passes the SANY parser. Include the MODULE declaration, EXTENDS, CONSTANTS, VARIABLES, Init, Next and Spec. Include all safety invariants and liveness properties described, and any fairness conditions mentioned. Output only the TLA+ specification.

System description: The module specifies a threshold-based, one-step Byzantine consensus algorithm (Algorithm 2 from Dobre and Suri, 2006), modeled over N processes with up to T Byzantine faults allowed by the algorithm and up to F actual faulty processes, under the assumption N > 3T ≥ 3F ≥ 0.

Each process holds a program counter ranging over statuses: initial values V0 or V1, sent states S0 or S1, decided states D0 or D1, undecided fallback states U0 or U1, and BYZ for faulty processes. Rather than tracking individual messages, the spec uses aggregate counters: nSnt0 and nSnt1 for messages broadcast by correct processes, nSnt0F and nSnt1F for messages injected by faulty processes, and per-process nRcvd0 and nRcvd1 for messages received. The four key actions are Propose (a process in V0 or V1 broadcasts its value and moves to S0 or S1), Receive (a process increments its received count up to the current sent totals), Decide (a process in S0 or S1 that has received at least N−T total messages decides D0 or D1 if one value reached that threshold, or falls back to U0 or U1 otherwise), and Faulty (a non-Byzantine process becomes Byzantine, incrementing nFaulty up to F). The temporal specification adds weak fairness on Propose, Receive, and Decide. The config checks TypeOK as an invariant and verifies two LTL validity properties: if all processes initially propose 0 they never reach U or D1 states, and if all propose 1 they eventually all leave U and D0 states. An additional liveness property AllDecideOne asserts every process eventually decides D1.
